topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the lecture on cancer causation and sets out what students should learn.

topics.label: Genetic origins and clonal evolution of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations arising in susceptible cells can support clonal evolution within a permissive microenvironment.

topics.label: Environmental cancer risks versus chance and inherited susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the contribution of environmental exposure to cancer risk against explanations based on chance or genetic predisposition.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections can drive carcinogenesis, with Burkitt lymphoma providing a detailed example.

topics.label: How environmental carcinogens damage DNA
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how environmental exposures produce DNA damage that can become cancer-driving mutations.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish mutational initiation from the promotion of tumour growth through a supportive cellular environment.

topics.label: Tissue and developmental specificity of carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the context of exposure determines susceptibility to carcinogens and place that specificity within the preceding account of cancer-causing mechanisms.

topics.label: Evidence and methods for assessing carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how evidence is gathered to identify carcinogenic exposures and the limitations of establishing their effects.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This closing draws together the lecture's conclusions about environmental cancer risks and their assessment through the lens of everyday risk–benefit decisions.
